blockers: Internal budget for H100 nodes unclear
notes: Company background: industrial reservoir operator with distributed edge sensors and operator consoles; heavy need for deterministic inference for control assistance.

High level ask: dedicated GPU reservation with explicit throughput guarantees for steady-state and burst windows. Target sustained min tokens/sec and measurable p99 latency for conversational prompts (seq len ~768) and telemetry query embeddings.

Throughput targets discussed on 2026-02-18 call: baseline sustained minimum 120,000 tokens/sec across the dedicated pool (customer-calculated expected qps), concurrency cap guidance: 48 concurrent sessions with fair-share queuing, burst policy: allow up to 200% of sustained throughput for 5 minutes (2x burst credits) then throttle to sustained levels.

Latency SLOs: p50 < 70ms per token, p95 < 150ms (seq len 128), p99 < 400ms (seq len 768) for text-generation endpoints on reserved capacity. Telemetry/embedding endpoints: p99 < 250ms for batch size <=64.

Reserved GPU plan: customer prefers H100 80GB nodes but willing to consider 8xA100-80GB as fallback. Initial reservation request: 12 H100-equivalent GPUs (expecting headroom for autoscaler) with optional burst pool of additional 4 GPUs for short windows.

Autoscaling and burst mechanics: wants explicit burst-credit accounting (carryover not required) and a documented failover policy to fallback model variants (smaller quantized models) when sustained capacity exceeds reservation. Requests that Redwood provide a 'burst reconciliation' report monthly showing peak minutes and credit usage.

SLAs & penalties: legal asked for throughput SLA clause — if sustained tokens/sec drops below agreed min for >30m during business hours, customer requests service credits tiered by % below min. Also wants a clause for concurrency starvation events and guarantees on preemption behavior.

Caching & optimizations: customer will enable KV/prefix caching where possible; requests guidance from Redwood Optimize on batching and quantization profiles to reduce required GPU count. Interested in explicit batching knobs and kernel-selection notes for H100.
Security/compliance: must run inside VPC with KMS-integrated keys, audit logs forwarded to their SIEM, and option for on-prem air-gapped deployment for disaster-recovery tests.

Cost sensitivity: willing to commit to a 24–36 month reservation if throughput guarantees and defined credit mechanics accepted; looking to avoid large surprise egress/overage bills — wants per-minute billing visibility.
Quotes from customer: 'We need hard guarantees for tokens/sec — operator workflows can't tolerate unpredictable tails.'

Internal Redwood asks captured: confirm H100 availability by region, define concurrency quota semantics (per-tenant vs per-route), produce sample SLA addendum language and a sample monthly burst usage report template.

Risk notes: procurement pushing for 36-mo to get discounts; exec sponsor needs proof of deterministic p99 before signing — propose 2-week POC with synthetic load tests and third-party telemetry capture.

Desired POC scope: 2-week dedicated reservation (4 H100-equivalent) with synthetic traffic that simulates 10k conversational sessions/day, run three ramp tests to validate min tokens/sec and burst handling, Redwood to provide instrumentation dashboard and raw traces.

Next negotiation items: finalize minimum tokens/sec metric definition (total pool tokens/sec vs per-node), specify measurement windows, and agree on outage credit formula. Legal to review sample addendum week of 2026-03-15.
